author: ojiudezue
title: v4.5.11 — AC Energy-Aware Ramp-Down (slice 1) + slice/2 split decision
summary: Tier 2 cycle that replaces the v3.8.3 'still hot despite cooling' AC reset trigger with an energy-aware overshoot detector (current <= target - 0.5°F AND kWh-rate sustained > zone-specific threshold). Adds a soft setpoint nudge action before hard reset escalation. Compressor protection: persistent daily cap + global min-interval gate that survives HA restart (Bug Class #11 + #33 caught in review). Master switch defaults OFF on first install — feature is invasive. Per-zone kWh threshold (3-ton defaults to 0.8 kW; user manually raises 4-ton's to 1.0). Shipped as 'slice 1' — observability sensors (D7, D8), diagnostic dump button (D10), and HC/EC user manuals (D11) deferred to v4.5.12 to get compressor protection live faster while observability is wrapped around 1 week of real-world data.

decisions.decision: Detection trigger flipped from 'current > target (still hot)' to 'current <= target - 0.5°F AND sustained kWh > threshold (overshoot + waste)'
alternatives_considered: Keep existing trigger and add kWh-rate as ADDITIONAL gate (would still miss the dominant Texas failure mode)
Use time-only sustained detection without kWh awareness (false positives on legit modulation)
Use kWh rate alone without overshoot gate (would fire during normal high-load cooling-toward-setpoint)
decisions.why: User's manual observation 2026-05-10: AC2 reached cooling setpoint, kept drawing >2 kWh past setpoint before manual off→on intervention restored normal cycling. The v3.8.3 detection (current > target) NEVER fires for this mode because the room is already cool. kWh as PRIMARY gate is what makes the detection meaningful — time-only triggers would false-positive on variable-speed Bryant's natural modulation near setpoint. The 0.5°F gap prevents flap when current_temp == target_temp_high during legit cycling (Bryant rounds to 0.5°F). 3-sample debounce + 10-min sustained gate eliminates noise.
decisions.implications: The legacy 'AC can't reach setpoint' failure mode (undersized AC, refrigerant low) is no longer detected automatically. That's acceptable for this single-user Texas install — the dominant failure is overcooling waste, not undercooling. If a future user reports the legacy mode, we'd add it back as a second detector path (different threshold semantics, different action).
decisions.revisit_trigger: If field data after 1 week shows the detection never fires despite known waste (user observation of AC behavior vs detection log), lower kWh threshold default OR drop the gap to 0°F. If false-positive rate >40% after threshold tuning, narrow the overshoot gap to 1°F.

decisions.decision: Soft + hard action ladder with hard reset gated by daily cap (2/day) AND global min-interval (2hr) — both required
alternatives_considered: Soft-only (no hard reset ever) — removes safety net if controller deeply hangs
Hard-only (skip soft nudge) — wastes compressor starts when soft would have worked
Single gate (daily cap only) — leaves day-rollover compressor-cycling vulnerability
Single gate (min-interval only) — no per-day cap means a stuck controller could fire 12+ resets/day
decisions.why: User direction: 'Actually soft + hard but I think if we do hard we have to klimit. how many times it can do it in a 24 hour period. The worst thing we can do is rapidly cycle a compressor because of an error'. Two gates AND together because each handles a different failure mode: daily cap = 'this controller is having a bad day, don't make it worse'; min-interval = 'never two starts within 2 hours, no matter what date the calendar says'. The min-interval gate's no-date-filter MAX query is the critical R2 mitigation — without it, a reset at 23:55 + day rollover + reset at 00:02 = 7-min compressor short cycle (warranty-voiding).
decisions.implications: Even worst-case 'feature broken, escalates every time' cannot produce more than 2 hard resets per day per zone, and never 2 within 2 hours. That's well within Bryant's published cycle-rate spec. Lockout flag + persistent notification surfaces the failure for human investigation when cap is hit. Tests assert the min-interval query has no `AND date =` clause.
decisions.revisit_trigger: If user reports lockout firing routinely (more than 1x/week), the kWh threshold is too sensitive — tune up before changing the cap. If a Bryant firmware update changes the compressor's safe cycle rate, revisit the 2-hour min-interval.

decisions.decision: Persistent state in SQLite (ac_reset_state + ac_ramp_events tables) — daily counters + in-flight nudge state survive HA restart
alternatives_considered: In-memory only (existing ac_reset_count_today pattern from v3.8.3) — restart loop bypasses caps
HA Storage helper JSON — simpler but not queryable for diagnostic reads
Single key-value table — wouldn't support the date-keyed rollover or efficient per-zone reads
decisions.why: User explicitly flagged: 'This all needs to survive restarts or we will not achieve the limits goal.' If `hard_reset_count_today` lives only in RAM, an HA restart at 11pm resets it to 0 — we could fire 2 more hard resets before midnight = 4 in 24h. Compressor protection requires durable state. SQLite already exists in URA (35+ tables in database.py), follows the established `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` pattern — no migration framework needed. Date-keyed primary key (zone_id, date) means rollover is automatic (new-day query returns 0 counter). Event log table enables future analytics + diagnostic dump (deferred to slice 2).
decisions.implications: Establishes ac_reset_state as the authoritative source for daily counters; ZoneState fields keep an in-memory mirror for legacy sensor compatibility but DB is source-of-truth. Future features that need per-zone-per-day persistence (vacancy stats, occupancy duration) should follow the same date-keyed pattern.
decisions.revisit_trigger: If ac_ramp_events table grows beyond reasonable for diagnostics (e.g., 50k+ rows during stress testing), tighten retention from 30 to 14 days. If SQLite write queue ever shows backlog warnings, batch the 3-writes-per-cycle into a single executemany.

decisions.decision: DB write happens BEFORE the climate.set_temperature service call in _perform_soft_nudge (R1 ordering)
alternatives_considered: Setpoint first, then DB write (more intuitive in code reading order)
Wrap both in a try/except with rollback on failure (still leaves Bryant at +1.5°F if process dies between)
decisions.why:
If HA crashes between the DB write and the service call: DB says 'nudge in flight, original=73' but Bryant is still at 73. Next startup audit reads DB, calls 'restore to 73' — which equals current target. No-op. Safe.

If we did setpoint first, then DB: Bryant is now at 74.5, then we crash before DB write. Next startup has no DB record. Bryant sits at 74.5 indefinitely until next nudge or manual intervention. Orphan drift.

DB-first ordering trades a tiny window of 'DB lies about state' for a much larger guarantee 'thermostat never silently drifts'. The lie-window is closed by the immediate-next-step (service call) which makes DB accurate. This is the canonical write-ahead pattern.
decisions.implications: Every future v4.5.x feature that issues HA service calls with persistent state implications must follow the same ordering: DB-first, service-second. Test asserts this ordering explicitly (test_db_write_BEFORE_setpoint_change).
decisions.revisit_trigger: Never. This is foundational. If someone proposes reordering 'for clarity' in a future review, reject and point them at this entry.

decisions.decision: Ship as 'slice 1' with detection + actions + persistence + master switch + buttons, defer observability (D7, D8) + diagnostic dump + user manuals (D11) to v4.5.12
alternatives_considered: Ship single mega-cycle with all 11 deliverables (~1400 LoC + ~6000-10000 words of docs + ~70 tests)
Ship slice 1 as just D1-D4 + master, defer all D5+ to next cycle (loses ability to USE the feature)
decisions.why: User direction: 'Option 2 is fine. I'm relying on the 2x review to spot check so just follow our quality protocols and don't skimp.' The compressor-protection critical path is the safety-essential piece; observability is critical for tuning but not safety. Splitting lets us: (a) deploy safety faster, (b) collect 1 week of field data before deciding observability defaults, (c) write user manuals against the REAL behavior we observe, not the hypothetical behavior we modeled. Slice 2 is informed by data, not assumed. This is the 'minimum viable safety + iterate on observability' pattern.
decisions.implications: v4.5.11 ships compressor protection. v4.5.12 wraps observability around what we learn. User cannot answer 'how often did this fire today?' from the UI in slice 1 — they SQL-query ac_ramp_events table for now. Acceptable for 1 week. Slice 2 is committed (not vague 'someday'), tracked in PLANNING_v4.5.11 'Out of Scope' section + a new follow-up task for v4.5.12 plan creation. README lists what's deferred + when it ships.
decisions.revisit_trigger: If slice 1 field data shows nudges firing rarely OR misclassifying frequently, accelerate slice 2 observability (need false_positive_rate sensor to tune). If field data validates the design cleanly, slice 2 can take its time.

decisions.decision: Per-zone kWh rate threshold slider (one per AC zone), everything else house-wide
alternatives_considered: All 7 sliders per-zone × N zones = 21 sliders (UX punishment)
All house-wide including threshold (forces 4-ton to use 3-ton threshold or vice versa)
decisions.why: User specified per-zone after I proposed it: 'Per zone. Two 3 tons. One 4 ton.' Threshold is the ONLY variable tightly coupled to AC tonnage (compressor minimum-modulation floor scales with rated kW). Nudge size, sustained samples, time gates, daily caps, min-intervals — those are algorithm/safety tuning that should be uniform house-wide. Making everything per-zone × 3 ACs = 21 sliders for marginal flexibility. Per-zone threshold = 3 sliders for the variable that actually varies.
decisions.implications: Per-zone storage lives on ZoneState.kwh_rate_threshold (not OverrideArrester instance attr). Factory pattern differs from house-wide factory — separate _hvac_zone_kwh_threshold_factory(zone_id, zone_name) that pushes to zone manager. Future per-zone tunables (if any) follow the same pattern. Defaults: 3-ton zones use 0.8 kW (25-30% of rated); user manually raises 4-ton's to 1.0 kW post-deploy via slider (no redeploy).
decisions.revisit_trigger: If user reports tuning struggles or wants to share AC tonnage at config time, add an AC tonnage form field that auto-suggests threshold (or computes threshold = tonnage × 0.25). Likely overkill for single-user.

decisions.decision: AST-walk import resolution test catches v4.5.10.1-class bugs during build (caught one during this cycle)
alternatives_considered: Only test that import statements look textually correct (v4.5.10's original approach — DIDN'T catch SIGNAL_HVAC_ENTITIES_UPDATE)
Skip import tests entirely (let runtime catch it on live HA)
Per-symbol targeted tests (v4.5.10.1's approach — works but doesn't generalize)
decisions.why: During v4.5.11 build, I imported CONF_ZONE_THERMOSTAT from domain_coordinators.hvac_const in _discover_ac_zones (both number.py + button.py). The constant actually lives in const.py. Test failed immediately, I fixed it. Without the AST-walk this would have shipped silently — same shape as v4.5.10 SIGNAL_HVAC_ENTITIES_UPDATE ImportError that DID ship to live HA. The pattern verifies 'imports RESOLVE, not just that they're textually present'. Worth promoting beyond test_v4511 — recommend adding to QUALITY_CONTEXT.md Bug Class #32 as the validated regression pattern. Could become a project-wide hook for all PRs.
decisions.implications: All future cycles get this protection automatically by adding the target file to the TestImportResolution suite. Establishes a pattern that scales: AST-walk every from-relative-import, follow to target module, source-grep for symbol definition. Three test methods in v4.5.11 already cover number.py + switch.py + button.py + hvac_override.py.
decisions.revisit_trigger: If a 3rd v4.5.x ImportError-class bug ships despite this test, the test has a false-negative — investigate. Until then, the test pattern is sound.

refs.what_prompted_this: User manual observation 2026-05-10: AC2 reached cooling setpoint, kept drawing >2 kWh past setpoint before user manually forced off→on. v3.8.3 AC Reset detection ('current > target') never fires for this mode.
